newsitem.title: UK: Mark leaps on Euro crosses on French poll jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mark leaps on Euro crosses on French poll jitters.

text.p: The mark leapt against other European currencies, setting a 17-week high against the French franc and an eight-week high against the Spanish peseta amid nervousness before the next round of French elections.

Rumours of a private opinion poll conducted in the run up to Sunday's second election round unsettled traders and initially triggered the mark's rise. Traders said any poll suggesting the opposition Socialists were widening their lead over the ruling right-wing coalition was bound to undermine the franc.
The German currency extended its gains amid rumours Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer was poised to resign, with a denial of such speculation doing little to dampen demand for marks.

"People are very jittery about things and seem to think buying marks is a one-way bet as long as the uncertainty about the French elections lasts," said Julian Jessop, the European economist at Nikko Europe.
"The resignation rumours were clearly nonsense, but logic seems to have gone out of the window for the time being."

The mark ratcheted above 3.38 marks for the first time since February 5 and was last at 3.3814/19 compared with 3.3756/61 late Tuesday in Europe. Mark/lira rose to 992.15, its highest since May 13 and last traded for 992.25/50 from 986.05/35 late yesterday. Mark/peseta clambered as high as 84.86/89, its strongest since April 1, from 84.37/39 yesterday.

While the mark's gains were met with intervention from Swedish and Spanish central banks, according to traders, analysts expect its rally to continue as long as uncertainty about the French elections persists. The Bank of France declined to comment on market rumours that it was also intervening to cap the mark's rise against its currency.
Traders expect more such intervention if the European crosses continue to move away from their central parities against the mark in the European exchange-rate mechanism.

The franc, which hasn't been more than 1 percent away from its 3.3539 per mark parity, was last trading 0.8 percent weaker than this rate. The lira is also about 0.8 percent away from its central ERM rate.

The political uncertainty which sparked the mark's rally today overshadowed speculation that a Socialist government in France would push for a broader European economic and monetary union than Germany would like.
"The French elections have totally confused market players and they are just waiting until Sunday's elections are out of the way," said a trader at a Japanese bank in London.
Concern that countries like Italy and Spain will be among the founders of EMU had weighed on the mark earlier this week and could yet resurface to undermine the German currency, analysts said.
Still, traders were more concerned for the time being with the chances that French calls for a broad monetary union would harden German opposition to the single currency project, analysts said.
"A broad EMU is theoretically positive for currencies like the lira and the peseta unless it strengthens the hand of those Germans who are arguing for a delay," said Jessop at Nikko.

The gap between the theoretical and the actual ecu widened to 0.46/51 from 0.25/28 on Friday, pointing to increased concern about EMU. The Swiss franc is expected by traders to be a key beneficiary of nervousness about monetary union, even though the Swiss National Bank has pledged to combat franc strength.

"The Swiss franc will be the beneficiary of euro turmoil and the SNB will be moving against very large flows," said a trader at a Japanese bank in London. "They can play around with money-market rates but that won't do much about the fear and uncertainty which will be driving the market."
Mark/Swiss was last at 83.37/39 centimes, from 83.40/41 late yesterday. -Swaha Pattanaik, London newsroom +44 171 542 6284
